assumptions.basis: assumed (not in the canonical WorldSmall files): LINERLIB benchmark documentation gives a minimum port stay of 24 h, a minimum transshipment time of 48 h and a bunker cost of 600 USD/t. transfer_wait_days is the expected wait for a connecting weekly departure (half a week).
assumptions.sailing_speed: class designSpeed (only speed with a source consumption)
assumptions.transit_time_unit: TransitTime column read as days (unverified unit)

assumption_register.name: Vessel capacity unit
assumption_register.value: Capacity FFE x 2 -> TEU (converted once at the loader)
assumption_register.source: LINERLIB reference code types the capacity as FFE (BM_Graph.hpp, bm_data.hpp); RL paper arXiv:2411.09068 App. A.1 agrees; the technical report text was not available
assumption_register.affects: capacity, coverage, profit levels (x1.6-2.5 against the TEU reading)

assumption_register.name: FFE -> TEU conversion
assumption_register.value: 1 FFE = 2 TEU exactly, no lane factors
assumption_register.source: definition of the units; lane factors removed (unsourced)

assumption_register.name: Transit-time limits
assumption_register.source: LINERLIB authors recommend the revised file; 13.0 % of demand differs; no decision recorded
assumption_register.affects: coverage of ODs whose limit differs (105 ODs)

assumption_register.name: TransitTime scope
assumption_register.value: end-to-end days including port stays and transfer dwell
assumption_register.source: unit reproduced from the upstream revision rule; inclusion of port time not stated by any source

assumption_register.name: Port stay per call
assumption_register.source: OR-tools LINERLIB benchmark page (minimum port stay 24 h); paper: 1 day

assumption_register.name: Transfer dwell
assumption_register.source: 48 h from the benchmark page; the 3.5 d wait is a model convention

assumption_register.name: Bunker price
assumption_register.source: benchmark page (600 USD/t); not a market price; fuel grade / fuel systems unverified

assumption_register.name: Fuel grade and vessel fuel systems
assumption_register.source: fleet file carries no fuel-system data

assumption_register.name: Service frequency granularity
assumption_register.value: integer departures per week, vessels = ceil(T f / 7)
assumption_register.source: no source defines the allowed frequencies; paper uses fractional vessels

assumption_register.name: Port cost units
assumption_register.value: CostPerFULL, CostPerFULLTrnsf are USD per FFE (divided by 2 -> per TEU); port call = fixed + PortCallCostPerFFE x vessel capacity per call
assumption_register.source: loader contract; no upstream sentence confirms the per-FFE reading

assumption_register.name: Canal fees (Suez, Panama)
assumption_register.value: charged: traversals of the closed rotation x class fee, once per weekly departure; blank fee = class cannot pass (never zero)
assumption_register.source: LINERLIB reference code calculate_canal_cost and the authors' WorldSmall solution log (34/34 traversal counts, cost within the log's rounding); fees are benchmark data, not a verified real tariff; owner countersign (D-08) outstanding
assumption_register.affects: cost of canal routes, class eligibility

assumption_register.name: Rejected-demand penalty
assumption_register.source: paper / benchmark use 1000 USD per rejected unit; operating profit excludes it by definition

assumption_register.name: Unused vessels
assumption_register.source: paper credits unused vessels at the time-charter rate

strategy_report.definition: strategies are the realised structure of the routed cargo, not quotas; see src/network/strategy_report.py

utilisation.capacity_unit: TEU (fleet file 'Capacity FFE' is FFE, converted x2 once by the loader; status reference_code)

contribution_margin.definition: revenue - cargo-variable costs (handling + transshipment + per-TEU port variable); vessel, fuel and port-call costs are the fixed service costs of the schedule

vessel_utilisation_teu.definition: carried TEU-legs / offered TEU-legs of the service a vessel sails (vessels of one service share its value); average = network total carried / offered; min / max over services; leg_min / leg_max over the individual legs

transit_time_days.definition: days per routed flow (an origin-destination path): sailing + port stays + transfer dwell; mean is TEU-weighted, mean_per_flow is unweighted; min / max over flows

transshipment.definition: TEU of flows that change service at least once; transfer_moves counts a container once per transfer (two transfers = two moves)

problem_analysis:
Size: Small
Complexity Drivers:
- High network density at 163.2% indicates significant route overlap and capacity contention across the 1,764 lanes.
- Low demand concentration with a Top-5 share of only 5.7% implies a highly distributed load profile requiring broad coverage.
- Moderate average lane demand of 156.7 TEU suggests many low-volume lanes that complicate service consolidation.
Demand Concentration: low - The dispersed demand profile necessitates a dense service network to maintain connectivity without relying on a few high-volume corridors.
Decomposition Rationale: The 47-port network should be partitioned into three regional clusters of approximately 15-16 ports each to manage the 163.2% density while preserving intra-regional lane integrity.

archetype_params.notes: Median demand of 98.0 TEU and total volume of 147,894 TEU support a hybrid model where 15% direct services handle high-volume lanes like CNYTN-USLAX (3,730 TEU) while 50% trunk services manage the remaining 99.5% of demand across 604 lanes, retaining approximately 120 of 800 candidates.

regional_results.strategy:
Strategy: C
Selected: hybrid
Reason 1: Median demand of 98.0 TEU/lane indicates fragmented volume requiring direct service for high-density lanes like CNYTN -> USLAX (3,730 TEU/wk) while maintaining hub consolidation for lower-volume routes.
Reason 2: The network comprises 14 ports and 604 lanes, creating a complex topology where a hybrid model optimizes the trade-off between the 7.2% top-3 share concentration and the remaining 92.8% distributed across 604 lanes.
Hub Ports: [CNSHA, MYTPP, CNYTN, HKHKG, CNTAO]

iteration_selection.reasoning: Iteration 2 is the only candidate that maximizes weekly profit ($47,508,842) and global demand-weighted coverage (48.5%) while maintaining a Pareto-optimal status. Although it has the highest total cost ($95,488,028), the incremental cost is justified by the $1,340,250 weekly profit increase over Iteration 1 and the reduction of unserved demand to 142,292 TEU/wk.
